description:
One shared table for the URL a citation is allowed to carry.

A citation is delivered twice: as the destination of an ordinary Markdown link every surface can follow, and as the `url` of a `message.content.citations` row. The Web renderer draws a badge only when the two agree exactly, so the backend has to write the destination the real Markdown pipeline (remark-parse -> remark-rehype's normalizeUri -> defaultUrlTransform) produces from it - a fixed point - and has to label it with the host a browser actually resolves.

Both sides of that boundary read this file: tests/test_citations.py asserts core.citations produces `url`/`label` from `raw`, and ui/src/components/ui/markdown.test.tsx renders `url` and asserts the DOM href and the WHATWG host come back unchanged. Neither side can drift without the other failing. `url: null` means the raw value must be rejected outright rather than repaired.

`authority` is the same table for the authority - userinfo, host and port - where the browser is the assertion rather than a reference: every accepted row's `url` is one `new URL` opens rather than refuses, and `new URL(url).hostname` is exactly that row's `label`. The authority stays as the provider wrote it - letter case, a leading zero in a port, an uncompressed IPv6 address - because each of those spellings opens the same page, and the label is where the browser's own answer is shown instead. A `url: null` row is one a browser refuses, apart from the single deliberate exception whose `why` says so. A new authority shape is a row here, not a branch.
